reasoning: Wrote index.html (~200 lines, vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no deps or network). Participants (name, IANA zone via datalist from Intl.supportedValuesOf, start/end time inputs default 09:00-17:00) can be added/removed; viewer zone defaults to the browser zone and is overridable. Every 30-min slot from the next half-hour boundary over 7 days (336 instants) is converted to each zone with Intl.DateTimeFormat.formatToParts (hourCycle h23), and kept if each participant local minute-of-day m satisfies start<=m and m+30<=end (or the wrapped test when end<start, i.e. shifts crossing midnight). DST/non-hour offsets fall out of Intl naturally; each cell shows the short zone name (e.g. GMT+5:30, EDT) so offset changes are visible, and a participant date is shown when it differs from the viewer date. State is in the hash as URLSearchParams (tz=...&p=name|zone|start|end) via history.replaceState, restored on load and hashchange. Native inputs/buttons with labels, aria-live results, focus rings, aria-invalid + error text for unknown zones; grid collapses to 2 columns and tables scroll horizontally under 640px. Opened in Chrome: verified Kolkata +05:30, Tokyo 22:00-06:00 shift, Pacific/Auckland DST start on Sep 27 (GMT+12 -> GMT+13, overlap shrank from 10 to 8 slots), add/remove updating the hash, and a ~640px layout. Known limitations: not tested on an actual phone or with a screen reader; no weekend filter; zone list falls back to a short hardcoded list on browsers without Intl.supportedValuesOf; the results table for many participants relies on horizontal scroll.
